description: EBA Guidelines on customer due diligence and factors credit and financial institutions should consider when assessing money laundering and terrorist financing risk associated with individual business relationships and occasional transactions. Updated 2021. Will be replaced by AMLA RTS from ~2026.

metadata.status: in force until replaced by AMLA

description: EBA Guidelines on internal governance under the Capital Requirements Directive. Includes AML/CFT governance requirements: management body oversight of AML risk, compliance function, internal audit, remuneration policy interaction with AML.

EBA guidelines on supervisory practices and AML/CFT supervision, promoting convergence across national supervisors. Covers risk-based supervision methodology, inspection planning, risk scoring, and supervisory college operation.

EBA guidelines specifying how AML/CFT risk should be factored into the Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process (SREP) under the CRD. Allows supervisors to require additional capital or other measures where AML risk materially impacts prudential safety.

EBA Guidelines on the assessment of the suitability of members of management body and key function holders. Includes AML/CFT criteria: persons must not have ML/TF convictions; ML/TF findings affect suitability determination.

EBA opinions and guidelines on the interaction between PSD2 and AML requirements. Covers: AML obligations of payment institutions, open banking data access restrictions for AML purposes, and SCA interaction with transaction monitoring.

The level of ML/TF risk associated with a business activity, product, service, customer type, or geographic area BEFORE application of controls and mitigation measures. Starting point for BWRA. EBA guidelines provide frameworks for inherent risk factor assessment.

The ML/TF risk remaining AFTER application of controls, CDD measures, and mitigation strategies. Residual risk should be proportionate to the entity's risk appetite. Gap between inherent and residual risk reflects effectiveness of controls.

EBA-prescribed BWRA methodology: (1) identify inherent risk across customer, product/service, delivery channel, and geographic risk factors; (2) assess effectiveness of controls; (3) determine residual risk; (4) document and review annually. Must be granular and specific.

Risk factors associated with the customer type as defined in EBA/GL/2021/02. Includes: type of customer (individual, corporate, trust, PEP), geographic origin, business sector, complexity of ownership structure, purpose of relationship.

Risk factors associated with specific products or services as defined in EBA/GL/2021/02. Includes: cash-intensive products, cross-border transfers, e-money, crypto-assets, private banking, anonymous features.

Risk factors associated with how products/services are delivered. Includes: face-to-face vs. non-face-to-face, internet/mobile-only relationships, use of introducers or agents, geographic delivery channel considerations.

Risk factors associated with geographic areas. Includes: FATF high-risk countries, EU HRTCs, jurisdictions with strategic AML deficiencies, offshore financial centres, countries with high corruption/crime indices, sanctioned countries.

EBA guidelines specify red flags for transaction monitoring: unusual transaction patterns, structuring below reporting thresholds, transactions inconsistent with customer profile, rapid fund movements through multiple accounts, geographic inconsistencies.

Process of assigning a risk score (e.g., low/medium/high) to each customer based on risk factors assessed during CDD. Must be documented. Must determine CDD intensity: SDD for low risk, standard CDD for medium, EDD for high risk. Must be reviewed periodically.

Proportionality principle in CDD: the depth and frequency of CDD measures must be calibrated to the assessed risk level. EBA guidelines require documented rationale for CDD calibration decisions. Cannot apply SDD to PEPs or HRTC customers.

National supervisors must report AML/CFT information to EBA, including: supervisory convergence data, breach notifications, cross-border cases involving EU-wide impact, and information on identified ML/TF risks. EBA publishes annual AML/CFT reports.

EBA coordinates AML/CFT supervisory colleges for cross-border institutions. National supervisors share information and coordinate supervisory actions. EBA ensures consistent approaches. Transitioning to AMLA from 2025.

From 1 July 2025, AMLA takes over EBA's AML/CFT guideline function. EBA guidelines remain valid as 'grandfathered' until replaced by AMLA RTS/ITS. Priority: AMLA RTS on risk factors (replaces EBA/GL/2021/02) and RTS on CDD standards.

AML/CFT considerations in fit & proper assessments: criminal record checks for ML/TF offences, regulatory history, experience in compliance/risk management. An ML/TF conviction or material finding is a strong indicator of unsuitability.

EBA emphasises proportionality in applying the RBA: smaller, simpler institutions may apply simplified BWRA methodologies while still demonstrating risk understanding. The substance of risk assessment must be adequate regardless of format.

canonical_name: EBA AML Guideline Scope — Credit & Financial Institutions
description: EBA AML guidelines apply to credit institutions and financial institutions as defined in AMLD4/AMLR. Do not apply to DNFBPs (lawyers, accountants, etc.) or non-EEA entities. AMLA guidelines will have same scope.

EBA's process for promoting consistent AML/CFT supervision across Member States: periodic convergence plans, thematic studies, peer reviews, supervisory college facilitation, and binding Q&A on guideline interpretation.

EBA-prescribed step-by-step BWRA process: (1) scope definition; (2) risk factor identification per category; (3) inherent risk scoring; (4) controls effectiveness assessment; (5) residual risk scoring; (6) documentation and senior management sign-off; (7) annual review.

Operational process for assigning and maintaining customer risk ratings: initial rating at onboarding, periodic review triggers (transaction anomalies, SAR filing, news events), enhanced review for PEPs, high-risk third countries, complex structures.

EBA/GL/2021/02 cross-references: Section 4 (business-wide RA) → AMLR Art. 10 (BWRA); Section 5 (CDD risk factors) → AMLR Art. 20-34 (CDD); Section 6 (simplified CDD) → AMLR Art. 31; Section 7 (enhanced CDD) → AMLR Art. 34.

canonical_name: EBA Guidelines → AMLA RTS Replacement Map
description: Mapping of EBA guidelines to planned AMLA RTS replacements: EBA/GL/2021/02 → AMLA RTS on Risk Factors; EBA/GL/2021/05 → AMLA RTS on Internal Governance; EBA supervisory convergence guidelines → AMLA ITS on Supervisory Methodology.

canonical_name: EBA Guidelines → FATF RBA Guidance Cross-Reference
description: EBA/GL/2021/02 is aligned with FATF's Risk-Based Approach Guidance for the Banking Sector (2014, revised). EBA guidelines translate FATF principles into EU-specific regulatory requirements.
